html:
The metro system of Cairo, opened in 1987. It was the first full metro in Africa and the Arab world.

Line 1, built with French help, joined old suburban railways with a tunnel under the city centre, running from Helwan in the south to the north. Line 2 followed in the 1990s, with a tunnel under the Nile, and Line 3 opened in stages from 2012, toward the airport.

Greater Cairo is one of the largest cities on earth, with roads jammed day and night. The metro carries millions of passengers a day, and fares were long kept very low. Each train has carriages for women only.

Station names follow politics. The central station named after Hosni Mubarak was renamed after the martyrs of the 2011 revolution, and the station under Tahrir Square is named after Anwar Sadat.
sum: The metro system of Cairo, opened in 1987. It was the first full metro in Africa and the Arab world.
